250 Massachusetts Ave NW, Suite 400 | Washington, DC 20001  
September 10, 2026 
VIA EMAIL 
Re: False Advertisement by CLF Regarding Janelle Stelson 
Dear Station Manager: 
We write on behalf of DCCC regarding an advertisement sponsored by the Congressional Leadership Fund 
(“CLF”) currently airing on your station. 1 This advertisement is false and deceptive. It claims that Janelle 
Stelson, a candidate for the U.S. House of Representatives, “support[s] a plan to close up to 25 Pennsylvania 
ssupported a plan to close rural hospitals, nor has she supported the policy the advertisement implies would 
have that consequence. Because CLF’s advertisement deceives your viewers, it should be removed from 
the air.  
CLF’s advertisement claims that Ms. Stelson “support[s] a plan to close up to 25 Pennsylvania rural 
hospitals.” An on- screen citation directs viewers to a study by Navigant, published on August 6, 2019. 2 
This study was funded by special interests in the healthcare industry, and there are serious doubts about its 
accuracy.3 However, even assuming that the study is reliable, the study offers no support for CLF’s claim 
that Ms. Stelson supports a plan to close rural hospitals.  
To summarize, the Navigant study shows that offering a government insurance program reimbursing at 
Medicare rates as a public option on health insurance exchanges could, under a specific set of circumstances 
and assumptions, put 25 rural hospitals in Pennsylvania at risk of closure. But Ms. Stelson has never said 
that she supports the policy the Navigant study analyzed. Indeed, the study, which is more than seven 
years old, predates Ms. Stelson’s entry into politics altogether. It therefore cannot reasonably be read to 
refer to policies Ms. Stelson has advocated on the campaign trail. 
CLF will no doubt attempt to salvage its credibility by pointing to statements Ms. Stelson has made about 
her desire to increase access to affordable health care for Pennsylvanians. But none of those statements 
come close to what CLF’s advertisement claims. The Navigant study’s conclusion that a public option could 
put rural hospitals at risk turns entirely on one assumption: that the public option reimburses providers at

2 Jeff Goldsmith & Jeff Leibach, The Potential Impact of a Medicare Public Option on U.S. Rural Hospitals and 
Communities: A Scenario Analysis, Navigant (Aug. 2019) [hereinafter “Navigant Study”], 
https://americashealthcarefuture.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/Navigant-Rural-Public-Option-FINAL-8.19.pdf.  
3 See, e.g., Victoria Knight, Fact Check: GOP Senate Ad Misrepresents Montana Governor’s Stance on Heath Care , 
Missoula Current (Aug. 24, 2020), https://missoulacurrent.com/fact-check-ad-health-care (quoting an expert stating 
that Navigant’s analysis “is almost surely wrong”); Amy Sherman, Trump’s Misleading Attack on Biden’s Health 
Care Plan, PolitiFact (Nov. 1, 2020), https://politifact.com/factchecks/2020/nov/01/donald-trump/trumps-
misleading-attack-bidens-health-care-plan (noting that the Navigant study “was commissioned by the Partnership for 
America’s Healthcare Future, a health industry coalition that opposes Medicare for All and a public option ”). 
September 10, 2026 
Page 2 
Medicare rates.4 Ms. Stelson has never said she supports a public option reimbursed at Medicare rates—or 
endorsed any specific reimbursement structure at all. If anything, she has disclaimed the model the study is 
built on: asked about her health care views, she stated that “I wouldn’t call it Medicare for All.” 5 The 
Navigant study itself concedes that “[s]everal  less-sweeping alternatives to Medicare for All” exist, and 
that relatively minor policy adjustments could protect rural hospitals from the downsides of a public option.6 
The Navigant study does not address the impact of those “less-sweeping alternatives,” or of any policy Ms. 
Stelson has actually described supporting. CLF should know this: In other races, claims based on the same 
Navigant study have been fact-checked false because the study is “based on broad assumptions that don’t 
accurately reflect” the candidate’s position on healthcare.7 
CLF’s advertisement claims that Ms. Stelson “support[s] closing 25 Pennsylvania rural hospitals” when 
she has never even endorsed a policy that could potentially have that effect. This blatantly deceives 
viewers. Your station is not obligated to air this false advertisement unedited. The rule that bars a station 
from censoring a political advertisement, and that in turn immunizes the station from liability for its 
content, applies to advertisements sponsored by a candidate's own campaign. It does not apply here.8 
 
CLF has no right to command the use of your station’s broadcast facilities,9 your station bears 
responsibility for the content of any advertisement it chooses to air,10 and you have a duty “to protect the 
public from false, misleading or deceptive advertising.”11 
 
Because the advertisement deceives viewers by telling them that Janelle Stelson supports a policy 
she does not, we ask that you remove the advertisement from your station. Please contact us as soon 
as possible at (202) 968-4671 or vmaras@elias.law to discuss. 
 
Sincerely, 
 
Courtney T. Weisman 
Victoria Maras 
Counsel to DCCC
